sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia. Kolkata is the cultural capital of India and the largest city in eastern India. All records needs_review.

places.name: Victoria Memorial
places.description: Monumental white Makrana marble building completed in 1921, built in memory of Queen Victoria. Now a museum housing 25 galleries with Mughal and colonial era artefacts, paintings and historical documents. The surrounding 64-acre garden is a major public space. Evening sound-and-light shows run on most evenings. Budget 1.5 hours.

places.name: Howrah Bridge
places.description: Iconic cantilever bridge over the Hooghly River connecting Kolkata with Howrah, built 1943. One of the busiest bridges in the world carrying 100,000+ vehicles and 150,000 pedestrians daily. No entry fee; best viewed from river ferries (Ghat crossings) or at dusk when lit up. The view from both banks at sunrise is excellent for photography.

places.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
places.description: Major Kali temple on the east bank of the Hooghly River, 20km north of central Kolkata. Built in 1855 by Rani Rashmoni, it is associated with mystic Ramakrishna Paramahamsa who lived and taught here. The 25-hectare complex includes 12 Shiva shrines and Radha-Krishna temple. Temple runs on darshan timings; very crowded on weekends and festival days.

places.name: Indian Museum, Kolkata
places.description: India's oldest and largest museum, founded 1814. 35 galleries spanning natural history, geology, Egyptian mummies, Mughal artefacts, Buddhist sculptures and a coin collection. One of Asia's most comprehensive collections. Budget at least 2 hours; the sculpture and archaeological galleries are highlights.

places.name: College Street
places.description: A kilometre-long stretch known as Boi Para (Book Market) — one of the largest second-hand book markets in the world. Hundreds of pavement stalls and bookshops sell textbooks, Bengali literature, rare editions and imported titles. The adjacent Coffee House (Presidency University) is a legendary intellectual gathering spot since 1876.

places.name: Kumartuli
places.description: Historic potters' quarter north of Sovabazar, where artisans have crafted clay idols for Durga Puja for centuries. The neighbourhood is most active Aug–Oct before the festival season; workshops open to visitors. Outside season the streets are quieter but workshops still visible. Best accessed on foot from Sovabazar metro station.
places.openingDays: Workshops open daily; most active Aug–Oct

places.name: Belur Math
places.description: Headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1899, on the west bank of the Hooghly River. The Sri Ramakrishna Temple's architecture blends Hindu, Islamic and Christian motifs to symbolise the unity of all religions. Peaceful riverfront campus; Swami Vivekananda's room is open to visitors.

places.name: Marble Palace
places.description: Extraordinary 19th-century mansion in North Kolkata, built 1835 by merchant Raja Rajendra Mullick. Filled with European paintings, sculptures (including originals by Rubens and Reynolds), Venetian mirrors, Belgian chandeliers and a personal zoo. Still occupied by the Mullick family. Free entry but advance permit required from the West Bengal Tourism office.
places.openingDays: Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun 10:00–16:00 (closed Mon and Fri)

places.name: Park Street Cemetery
places.description: One of the oldest cemeteries in Asia (1767), containing elaborate Gothic, neoclassical and obelisk tombs of 18th–19th century Europeans who died in British India. Well-maintained; a peaceful and surprisingly beautiful space of historic architecture with fascinating inscriptions. Heritage walk starting point.

places.name: Botanical Garden, Kolkata
places.description: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden — established 1787, one of the world's oldest and largest botanical gardens at 109 hectares. Home to the Great Banyan Tree, considered the world's largest living tree by canopy area (340m circumference). Over 12,000 specimens; also a major research institution.

places.name: Kalighat Kali Temple
places.description: Ancient Shakti Peetha temple, one of 51 in India, where the right toe of Sati is said to have fallen. The current temple dates to 1809 though worship here is ancient. Kolkata (Calcutta) derives its name from Kalighat. Very popular pilgrimage site; expect long queues on auspicious days. Non-Hindus may not enter the inner sanctum.

places.name: Eden Gardens
places.description: India's oldest and most famous cricket ground (1864), with a 68,000-seat capacity making it one of the largest cricket stadiums in the world. Hosts international Test, ODI and IPL matches. Exterior is freely visible from surrounding public roads; stadium tours available on non-match days. The adjacent Maidan provides context for the colonial-era sporting landscape.
places.openingDays: Open for matches and tours; match schedule varies

places.name: Kolkata Kathi Roll — Park Street
places.description: Kolkata invented the kathi roll — a roti wrapped around egg, chicken, or paneer with onions, chutney, and lime. Nizam's (1932) is the original. Other greats: Kusum Rolls on Park Street. A handheld meal eaten walking — quintessential Calcutta street culture.

places.name: Kolkata Rosogolla and Mishti Doi
places.description: West Bengal's most iconic sweets: rosogolla (soft white sponge balls in sugar syrup) and mishti doi (sweetened fermented yoghurt in clay pots). Balaram Mullick & Sons (est. 1885) and K.C. Das (originators of industrialised rosogolla) are legendary. Essential Kolkata food experience.
places.area: Multiple — Bhowanipore, College Street, New Market

places.name: Kolkata Biryani at Arsalan
places.description: Kolkata biryani (Nawabi style) features a potato — a unique adaptation made when Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta. Arsalan, Royal, and Shiraz are the pilgrimage restaurants for this biryani style. The potato absorbs saffron and meat juices beautifully.
